title: Cognitive-Load Probing: Dual-Task Interference as a Deception Tell

original_idea.body:
# Cognitive-Load Probing: Dual-Task Interference as a Deception Tell

**Problem:** Lying is more cognitively demanding than truth-telling. If an agent secretly pursuing a side task is under extra load, that load might leak into degradation on a concurrent benign task.

**Direction:** Adapt the dual-task paradigm. Compare an open model's secondary-task performance/latency when honestly doing only the main task vs also covertly pursuing a hidden side task. Measure detectable degradation.

**Why it matters:** Tests whether a classic human deception signature transfers to LLM agents, offering a behavioral sabotage tell that survives CoT obfuscation. Pure behavioral eval.

**Relevant context:** Cognitive-load deception (Vrij); SHADE-Arena (arXiv:2506.15740).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a behavioral sabotage tell surviving CoT obfuscation is valuable; the cognitive-load analogy is suggestive.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Behavioral eval comparing dual-task performance; inference-only, beginner-feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused degradation measurement; depends on constructing matched honest/attack conditions.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open model organism, no internal access; behavioral-tell work labs underweight.

novelty.reasoning: Cognitive-load deception theory classic; transfer to LLM-agent behavioral tells plausibly novel-ish.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Deception theory exists; LLM dual-task transfer plausibly open.
